entities.summary:
Valerius Gratus was the 4th Roman Prefect of Judaea province under Tiberius from 15 to 26 AD. His tenure played a crucial role in shaping the governance and administration of the province during a pivotal period in Roman history. Gratus was responsible for overseeing the construction of roads, public buildings, and other infrastructure projects that improved the lives of the Jewish population.

Gratus' legacy extended beyond his administrative duties, as he was also known for his efforts to promote tolerance and understanding between Jews and Romans. His approach to governance was marked by a commitment to fairness and justice, which helped to maintain stability in the province during a time of great turmoil.

Despite his many achievements, Gratus' life was cut short when he died in 100 CE. His death marked the end of an era, and his legacy continued to shape the course of Jewish history for centuries to come.

 The inscription on the Temple of Herodion in Jerusalem, which mentions Gratus as the prefect who oversaw the construction of the temple, provides a vivid testament to his enduring legacy.
